chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
that he was asked about vegetables/greenery: is there zakat on them even if they are sold for great wealth? So he said: No, until a year passes over it.

key_terms.الحول: Al-hawl — the passage of one complete lunar year, a prerequisite for zakat on most forms of wealth
key_terms.الخضر: Vegetables, greens, or fresh produce — perishable crops that do not survive the passage of a year
key_terms.زكاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam

ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory on vegetables and fresh produce in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) issues a clear legal ruling that zakat is not obligatory on vegetables and other perishable produce, regardless of the high price they may fetch. The ruling hinges on the hawl — the passage of one full lunar year — which is a prerequisite for zakat to become due on wealth. Since vegetables are perishable and typically consumed quickly, they do not meet this condition, and thus no zakat is owed on them.
